text:
PagerDuty Bot: :rotating_light: page fired: INC-82742 - inference-serving-5xx-rate - P1 - eu-west-1 - Affected customers: several; symptom: elevated 5xxs from model-hosting pool. Link: <https://pagerduty.com/incidents/INC-82742|INC-82742>
Ivy Chen: oncall here, claiming via PD. I’ll take ownership for now. @Samir @Ryan_H please standby.
Samir Patel: acked on PD, grabbing logs now. initial thought: spike in redis timeouts? seeing connection reset errors in host logs.
Ryan_H: I can try a rolling restart of the inference pool if we confirm it's a worker-side stuck conn issue. prepping command.
Jamie: metrics mid-1m: request_5xx_rate spiked to 12% at 09:12UTC, latency 95p increased by ~400ms. throughput steady.
Nora (Customer Success): we got 2 customer reports (acct: zeta-inc, atlas-ops) about failed requests. flagging potential SLA impact.
Ivy Chen: marker: customer impact = degraded for multi-tenant hosted customers in eu-west-1. Not full outage but increased error rate.
Samir Patel: dumping a quick grep of worker logs: ```grep -E "(ERR|Timeout)" /var/log/inference/* | tail -n 80``` seeing many `RedisConnectionError: read timeout` and `KVCacheMiss` churn.
SRE Runbook Bot: Suggested next steps: 1) Check Redis replication lag (redis-cli info replication) 2) Temporarily shift traffic to eu-central or use fallback routing 3) Scale inference workers by +20% 4) Enable short-circuit for non-critical low-priority queues.
Ryan_H: running scaling command now: ```kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-pool-eu-west --replicas=12```
Jamie: while that runs, can someone run a quick health-check from the LB? ```curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}
" https://eu-west.api.redwood.example/health```
Samir Patel: did redis-cli info replication — slave lag ~5000ms spikes; master CPU near 95% on one node. Looks like Redis is the choke.
Ivy Chen: decision: failover redis shard to standby, and shift some read traffic to standby. @Ryan_H can you coordinate with infra to trigger failover? I'll coordinate PD notes and customer comms.
Ryan_H: initiating failover (standby promotion) via internal tool: ```infractl redis promote --shard=shard-7 --confirm``` posted command to ops-bridge.
SRE Runbook Bot: Promotion request accepted; expected DNS propagation ~30s. Watch for reconnect storms. Consider staggered reconnects.
Jamie: after promote, 5xx rate started falling: now at 3.1% and trending down. latency 95p decreased ~180ms.
Nora (Customer Success): updating affected customers: brief note sent to zeta-inc and atlas-ops: "we're mitigating a backend cache issue; partial errors observed; ongoing mitigation; will update in 30m".
Samir Patel: post-promote logs show reconnect attempts but successful; some transient 503s as workers rehydrate cache.
Ivy Chen: rolling back scaling to baseline once stable. leaving a sticky note to follow up: run redis capacity tuning and add an alert for replication-lag > 2000ms.
Ryan_H: scaled back deployment to replicas=9. command: ```kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-pool-eu-west --replicas=9```
Jamie: scheduling a post-incident check: run evals against common prompt sets to ensure quality not regressed.
Ivy Chen: tagging this PD incident as "ack claimed -> mitigation performed -> partial customer impact -> resolved via redis failover". Will mark resolved on PD once we confirm 15m stable.
Nora (Customer Success): customer follow-up planned. No escalations requested yet.
Samir Patel: leaving runbook task: "investigate root cause of surge leading to redis CPU spike" assigned to infra team.
PagerDuty Bot: INC-82742 status updated: acknowledged by Ivy Chen.
Ivy Chen: last check 09:18UTC: 5xx rate stable at ~1.2%. I'm going to watch for 15m then resolve. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
